title: Change-the-band bosses and a Class Z scale night
summary: Hodes tells stories about bosses who change the band when business is down. He tells one boss to tear up his name after a night's pay of $17.15.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And this is the thinking, the typical thinking of bosses. Another story was working the Sahara. And the boss is sitting at the bar with a girl. And I heard that story.

Now, he was at least an aware boss about this music. This is the story I got. He asked this the waitress girl, 'what's wrong with the business?' She says, 'don't you know? It's the band.' The band gets fired. It's another old story. The guy goes next door to the band that's doing business, he says, 'how you guys doing?' 'Oh, man, we're doing all right.' 'I'm not doing so good.' 'Well, why don't you change the band?' First thing, change the band.
So I'm running into this change-the-band, work two weeks, work a week. If the cash register don't ring, the boss is not interested in the music that he's going to stick out,

And it's just a bad scene and we've got to put in seven hours. So, 9:00 to 4:00, we drive back to that same restaurant and he buys me a hamburger and he pays me a Class Z scale. After he's taken out Social Security. I got something like $17.15. And I'm not going to get -- and I've got to pay my fare both ways. And I'm not going to get home til about 7:00 in the morning. I says to him, 'do me a favor.' He says, what? I says, 'you know, you got my name on a piece of paper? Take it and tear it up. I can't afford to know you. Tear it up. Don't call me, just tear it up.'

And that was it. I never worked for him again, he never called me or nothing, which saved me. But this is another scene that I would run into with these kind of jobbing things. But little by little, people got to know, not the musicians, especially, or the owners, but lay people got to know that I was available. And if they had a wedding on a Saturday, they could get me. They didn't have to worry because I'd be available.
